subject: Calculating sample size for meta-analyzed GWAS

messages.author: 80171ab3d7adb6ab
messages.subject: Calculating sample size for meta-analyzed GWAS
parts:
To all,
I used MTAG to meta-analyze PGC AUDIT-P (quasi-continuous score, N=121604) and PGC-AUD (Walters)  (binary, N = 28757, Neff = 23925) - resulting in 2 separate GWAS (trait 1: AUDIT-P informed by AUD; trait 2 AUD informed by AUDIT-P).

I was going to use the second in a common factor model with SNPS.  The MTAG GWAS equivalent for the second trait was Nmax = 88231.  

(I looked at Hatoum et al (2022) (supplementary methods) for some clarification - for the MTAG of cig per day and the Fagerstrom score resulting in 1 GWAS -  I think they used MTAG GWAS equivalent N here; for the PAU, not done with MTAG, they added Neff to N of AUDIT-P.  Neither directly on point) 

(1) Would I use the MTAG GWAS equivalent Nmax or add AUDIT-P N to AUD Neff (145429)?  

(2) For the common factor model, would I consider the MTAG AUD binary. 

(3) If binary, then would I further calculate an Neff for use in common factor, based upon Nmax = 88231 (or the 143429) based up a sample proportion from the original PGC AUD GWAS?

Thanks in advance for your advice.
